summary: This excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel (Book 11, part 12, presented as fiction) describes life on Randall's farm, where the children are free to grow and educate themselves. Hannah develops steadily through outside pressure and becomes her mother's dependable helper, while Rebecca grows from within, amusing her family with pranks and imaginative play but seen as irresponsible and lacking common sense. Aurelia, the mother, favors Hannah because she relies on her for household and farm burdens, leaving Rebecca overlooked as a serious presence.
one_line: At Randall's farm, Rebecca's inner growth and playful pranks are contrasted with Hannah's dependable, careworn diligence, which wins their mother's favor.
key_facts: The children at Randall's farm grew, worked, fought, and educated themselves for nine months of the year, each in his own way.
Hannah was painstaking, humdrum, and limited, and could only have been developed by forces applied from without.
Rebecca needed nothing but space to develop in and a knowledge of terms to express herself, and grew always from within outward.
Rebecca's forces had seemingly been set in motion when she was born and moved of their own accord, towards what no one knew, least of all Rebecca herself.
Rebecca's creative outlets were limited to making bread, parting Fanny's hair in different positions, and playing fantastic pranks on the children.
Rebecca amused her mother and family but was never counted of serious importance and was never thought superior in any way despite being considered smart and old for her age.
Aurelia's experience of genius, as exemplified by the deceased Lorenzo de Medici, led her to greater admiration of plain, every-day common sense.
Aurelia had seven children and an income of fifteen dollars a month.
Hannah was her mother's favorite, and at fourteen was companion and partner in all her mother's problems.
Hannah kept the house while Aurelia busied herself in barn and field.
Rebecca was capable of set tasks such as keeping small children from harm, feeding poultry, picking up chips, hulling strawberries, and wiping dishes, but was thought irresponsible.
Aurelia, needing somebody to lean on, leaned on Hannah.
Hannah was a trifle careworn in face and sharp in manner, but was self-contained, well-behaved, and dependable.
